coach_says: Your anaerobic load is well above target (1009 vs 837 max) while both aerobic buckets are on point, so this week Tuesday's committed double carries all the intensity and everything else stays firmly aerobic. TSB is positive (+8) and HRV balanced, but your rising resting HR and moderate readiness (52) say don't stack extra hard work on top. Watch that resting HR trend — if it keeps climbing through midweek, swap Friday's long ride for a shorter Z2 spin and tell me.

days.session: Easy Z2 road spin (best weather day)
days.details: Total 60 min | Primary objective: aerobic maintenance and leg-opener before Tuesday's double | Zone 2, RPE 3-4, conversational throughout. Outdoor road ride before work — Monday is the driest day of the week, so enjoy it. Flat to rolling route, high cadence (90-95rpm), no surges, no sprints for signs. Finish feeling like you did nothing. This keeps you fresh for tomorrow's committed hard day.

days.session: Double day: AM hills + PM hard MTB group
days.details: AM (before work, ~60 min): Committed hills road ride. Rain forecast — mudguards and lights, or ride the climbs on the trainer if conditions are dangerous. Total 60 min | Objective: sustained climbing strength | 3-4 climbs at Zone 3-4 (RPE 6-7), seated, controlled — do NOT sprint the tops; your anaerobic load is already over target, so make these steady threshold efforts, not attacks. Z1 recovery between climbs. || PM (~90 min): Committed hard MTB group ride, non-negotiable. Ride it as it comes, but where the group allows, sit in rather than animating — you don't need more anaerobic spikes this week. Fuel well between sessions: carbs at lunch and a snack 60-90 min before the evening ride.

Warmup: 200m easy freestyle, focus on long exhale and relaxed stroke. Main set: 4x100m easy freestyle with 20s rest (RPE 3, no clock-chasing) + 4x50m drill (25m catch-up drill / 25m easy swim) with 15s rest. Cooldown: 100m very easy backstroke/breaststroke mix. Total: 900m. Purpose: pure recovery from Tuesday's double — blood flow, zero load on the legs. Rain and wind outside make the pool the right call. If you feel wrecked, cut the main set in half or swap for 30 min gentle yoga.

Warm-up: 8 min — bike erg easy 4 min, then glute bridges 2x10, banded lateral walks 2x10/side, bodyweight single-leg RDL 1x8/side. Main: RomanianDeadlift 3x8 (moderate load, ~70% effort — deliberately not maxed, long ride tomorrow) | BulgarianSplitSquat 3x8/leg (dumbbells, controlled tempo) | SingleLegGluteBridge 3x10/leg | PallofPress 3x10/side | SidePlank 3x30s/side. Rest 90s between strength sets, 60s on core. Objective: posterior chain strength and hip stability to support climbing power — loads kept moderate so your legs are ready for Friday's endurance ride. No heavy quad-dominant work today.

Total 2h50 | Primary objective: aerobic base volume — this is the biggest ride of the week | Zone 2 throughout, RPE 3-4, HR capped below top of Z2. Cooler and mostly dry — dress in layers and pack a rain jacket for possible drizzle. Rolling terrain fine, but stay seated and steady on rises — no threshold spikes, no town-sign sprints (protecting that anaerobic budget). Cadence 85-95rpm. Fuel from the start: 60-80g carbs/hour, drink to thirst. Discipline on the easy end is the whole point of this session.

Warm-up: 8 min — row erg easy 4 min, hip openers, bird-dogs 2x8/side, bodyweight squats 2x10. Main: TrapBarDeadlift 3x6 (moderate-heavy, leave 2 reps in reserve — Sunday's ride is easy so you can load a touch more than Thursday) | StepUp 3x8/leg (dumbbells, knee-height box, drive through the heel) | NordicCurlNegative 3x5 (or SwissBallLegCurl 3x10) | DeadBug 3x10/side | FarmerCarry 3x40m heavy. Rest 2 min on deadlifts, 90s elsewhere. Objective: progressive strength stimulus for the posterior chain and hamstring durability — the eccentric hamstring work protects you on the MTB. Optional: 15-20 min gentle yoga in the evening if you feel tight.

Total 2h | Primary objective: aerobic volume with skills, keeping the week fun and varied | Zone 2, RPE 3-4. Flowing trails rather than punchy technical climbs — walk or granny-gear anything that would force an anaerobic surge. Overcast with possible drizzle: pick trails that drain well and take a shell. This caps a solid aerobic week without adding intensity. Check in Monday morning: if resting HR is still trending up despite the easy back half of this week, next week starts with a lighter loading pattern.
